stemBlocks.value: The area of a rectangle is x² + 9x + 20 cm². (a) Factorise the expression completely. (b) Hence write down a possible expression for (c) the length and (d) the width. (e) Calculate the perimeter of the rectangle.
Think first: Area of a rectangle is length × width, so the two factors of the area expression are the two sides.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p094-q21 from workbook page 94.

solutionSteps.instruction: Find two numbers with product 20 and sum 9.
Match the factors to the sides, taking the larger bracket as the length.
Add the length and the width.
Double that sum to get the perimeter.

strategyBlocks.value: Factorise the area into two brackets, read those brackets as the length and the width, then add them and double for the perimeter.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) (x + 4)(x + 5)  (c) length = (x + 5) cm  (d) width = (x + 4) cm  (e) perimeter = (4x + 18) cm

whyThisWorks.value: Multiplying the two side lengths of a rectangle reproduces its area, so any pair of factors of the area expression is a valid pair of sides. Factorising therefore reverses the area calculation. The perimeter formula P = 2(l + w) then works with algebraic sides exactly as it does with numbers.

commonErrors.misconception: Giving the perimeter as (x + 5) + (x + 4) and forgetting to double it.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Giving the perimeter as (x + 5) + (x + 4) and forgetting to double it.
Avoid this: Doubling only one bracket: 2(x + 5) + (x + 4).

commonErrors.misconception: Writing the perimeter with cm² instead of cm — perimeter is a length.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing the perimeter with cm² instead of cm — perimeter is a length.

examTip.value: Keep track of units as you go: an area is in cm², its factors and the perimeter are in cm. A units slip loses easy marks even when the algebra is right.
